messages:
Alex (SRE): IncidentBot alerted: sudden auth_failures spike + abnormal /v1/generate pattern from ~1200 unique IPs in the last 2m. Error rate up 18%. paging oncall now. https://observability.example/redwood/alerts/1948001234
IncidentBot: Pager sent to #incidents-oncall (rotation: nisha). Priority: P1.
Nisha (Prod Ops): I'm on it. seeing a 10k rps fanout to /v1/generate, many short-lived sessions. logs show repeated username enumeration attempts.
Mike (Support): any customer impact flagged? CX queue quiet but rate limits are firing for some orgs.
Alex (SRE): Partial. a handful of orgs hit user-level token throttles and got 429s. Overall throughput degrading; backend tail-latency climbing.
Priya (Security): sounds like credential-probing + scraper farm. recommend immediate throttles and targeted WAF blocks.
Kai (Infra): I'll stage a temporary global rate-shape on edge LB: reduce per-ip rps to 8 with aggressive connection limits, apply SYN backoff. will also push a per-route token-based cap for /v1/generate.
Nisha (Prod Ops): do we want to disable batch endpoints? those amplify cost.
Jorge (Product): disabling batch will hurt customers dependent on batch ingestion for embeddings. prefer rate-shape first, then disable if necessary.
Alex (SRE): Agreed. plan: 1) apply ego rate-shape at lb 2) add WAF rule for clear bot signatures/IPs 3) temporarily tighten per-customer request quotas for free tier 4) monitor 5m and escalate.
Kai (Infra): applying rate-shape now. command: ```
# edge rate-shape
route: /v1/generate
limit: 8 rps per source.ip
burst: 3
penalty: 60s
```
Deploy Bot: rate-shape config deployed to edge cluster-3 in ~30s (deploy id dpl_87321).
Nisha (Prod Ops): applying temporary org quota reductions for free-tier and unverified orgs: -50% qps. Doing a rolling update to quota-service.
Deploy Bot: quota-service update succeeded (cfg q_2026_03_15_v1).
Priya (Security): pushing WAF ruleset: block requests with header patterns matching known scraping toolchains + block traffic from ASN lists A1,A2,A3. WAF rule id: waf_7201.
Deploy Bot: WAF rule waf_7201 applied (edge nodes: 12/12).
Alex (SRE): logs after rate-shape + WAF: auth_failures down 65%, overall rps down 40%. tail-latency improving. still seeing persistent small spike from a set of IP ranges.
Kai (Infra): adding IP denylist for remaining abusive CIDRs. command: ```
# add to edge denylist
ipset add denylist 203.0.113.0/24
ipset add denylist 198.51.100.0/23
```
Deploy Bot: ipset updates propagated to all edges.
Mike (Support): starting draft customer notice for impacted customers: short blurb about increased 429s due to automated abuse and mitigation steps. cc: legal.
Jorge (Product): include ETA for rollback of aggressive throttles (T+3h) and link to status page.
Nisha (Prod Ops): watchlist: key customers flagged for manual override if false-positive. list being compiled.
Priya (Security): recommend follow-up: 1) trace credential-stuffing source for takedown 2) add challenge (captcha) for suspicious sessions 3) improve fingerprinting.
Alex (SRE): Captcha/Circuit-breaker is a product change; for now we've reduced immediate blast radius.
IncidentBot: oncall handoff scheduled in 45m to next rotation (kai).
Nisha (Prod Ops): good improvement. metrics stable for 6m. keeping throttles in place and starting gradual relaxation test: bump per-ip rps to 12 for safe nets.
Kai (Infra): relaxation rolled to safe nets. monitor for 10m.
Alex (SRE): Action items captured: (1) Security to investigate ASN ownership + file abuse reports (Priya) (2) Product to coordinate captcha/workflow (Jorge) (3) SRE to run post-incident runbook and perf regression checks (Alex/Nisha) (4) Support to notify affected customers and track RCAs (Mike).
Priya (Security): beginning ASN takedown outreach. sending initial abuse report email.
Mike (Support): sent customer notices to 18 orgs that saw 429s, added link to status page.
Alex (SRE): summarizing for postmortem: attack >10k rps, mixed credential probes + lightweight scraping, mitigations: edge rate-shape, WAF rules, ip denylist, quota tightening. outcome: user-facing 429s for a subset of free-tier users; no data exfiltration detected.
Jorge (Product): want an exec summary for tomorrow's stand. will draft.
IncidentBot: thread closed automatically after 30m of inactivity.
Nisha (Prod Ops): handing off to Kai for next rotation. last check: metrics green.
Kai (Infra): I'm oncall now, keeping throttles for 2h then will evaluate further.
Alex (SRE): thanks team. postmortem owner: Alex. timeline: initial alert -> mitigations in 9m -> stabilization in 12m.
